note: Language Neutral URL Aliases forces every path_alias to be saved language-neutral (langcode = und / LANGCODE_NOT_SPECIFIED). Real mechanism: a decorator on path_alias.repository (service language_neutral_aliases.repository_decorator, priority 9) forces lookups to und; hook_entity_type_alter swaps path_alias storage to NeutralPathAliasStorage (create()/save() force langcode=und) and list builder to NeutralPathAliasListBuilder; hook_module_implements_alter runs last and unsets path's entity_translation_create. No config/UI/permissions/Drush. Behaviour is directly observable on the live site: any alias created ends up with langcode 'und' even if another langcode is requested. Medium introspection reads back the stored langcode of a known alias; hard execution creates an alias and verifies it is stored language-neutral. Fixtures use /lna-* source paths.

evals.prompt: What does the language_neutral_aliases module change about how Drupal stores URL aliases, and what langcode do aliases end up with?
evals.expected_output: It decouples URL aliases from the language system so every path alias is saved language-neutral (langcode = und / LANGCODE_NOT_SPECIFIED), making the same alias apply in all languages.

evals.prompt: Technically, how does language_neutral_aliases force aliases to be language neutral? Name the two core mechanisms (there is no settings form).
evals.expected_output: It decorates the path_alias.repository service to force lookups to LANGCODE_NOT_SPECIFIED, and via hook_entity_type_alter swaps the path_alias storage class to NeutralPathAliasStorage (create()/save() force langcode=und) plus a neutral list builder; it also unsets path's entity_translation_create hook.

evals.prompt: After installing language_neutral_aliases on an existing multilingual site, what happens to URL aliases that were already language-specific, and how do you convert them permanently?
evals.expected_output: Existing non-neutral aliases become hidden (they don't resolve, don't show on node edit, aren't listed) but are not deleted, so uninstalling restores them. To convert permanently, bulk-update them, e.g. UPDATE path_alias SET langcode = 'und' WHERE langcode <> 'und';.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a URL alias whose source (system) path is /lna-src-a. Inspect the live path_alias entity for that source and report the langcode it is stored with.
evals.expected_output: The alias for /lna-src-a is stored with langcode 'und' (LANGCODE_NOT_SPECIFIED), because language_neutral_aliases forces all aliases language-neutral.

evals.prompt: On this site an alias was created for the source path /lna-src-b while explicitly requesting the English (en) language. Inspect the live path_alias entity for /lna-src-b and report which langcode it was actually saved with.
evals.expected_output: It was saved with langcode 'und', not 'en' — NeutralPathAliasStorage::save() overrides any requested langcode to LANGCODE_NOT_SPECIFIED.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site (which runs language_neutral_aliases), create a URL alias mapping the system path /lna-task-source to the alias /lna-task-alias. Save it to the live site. It must end up language-neutral as this module requires.
evals.expected_output: A path_alias entity exists with path=/lna-task-source, alias=/lna-task-alias and langcode=und (creating it through the normal path_alias storage neutralizes the langcode automatically).

evals.prompt: On this site the URL alias for the system path /lna-fix-source is currently stored with a non-neutral langcode (en), left over from before language_neutral_aliases was in effect. Make that alias language-neutral (langcode und) as the module intends, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The path_alias for /lna-fix-source now has langcode=und (e.g. load it and re-save it — NeutralPathAliasStorage::save() forces und — or set its langcode to und directly).
